rv.q: The emancipation of slaves is not far away, but nor can it come quickly enough. So Ginnie does what she must to protect her children.
It's a thoughtful, touching, intelligent, funny and disarmingly gentle drama with strong roles for Black actresses.
Blood of my Blood brings an intimate dimension to a story about ancestry and the histories that carry us forward.
At the opening of Blood of my Blood, Talulah (Jodie Campbell) sings 'You got a right to the tree of life'. She is a young Black British woman who has come to South Carolina to conjure her ancestor.

cn.t: Debut playwright Joy Nesbitt delivers a striking, excellent drama that grips from the start, weaving together dual timelines of 1862 slavery and present-day to explore ancestry, power, and capitalism with an intriguing new voice.

ru.inst: £15 tickets for Monday performances released Mondays at 9 AM via show website.
